focus_areas: Bill color consistency with breeding status (Yellowish vs Black)
Feather boundary sharpness against blurred background
Species distinction from Chaffinch based on bill/plumage combo
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the bill color. The plumage suggests a breeding male (black head, orange breast), but the bill is yellowish-grey rather than black. Determine if this is a valid biological variation (e.g., early breeding season) or an AI inconsistency. Also, scrutinize the transition between the white wing bars and the black wing feathers for any signs of digital smearing. Crucially, inspect the feet for any 'melting' into the soil/leaf litter, as this is a common AI artifact in ground-dwelling birds.
image_description: A small passerine bird, appearing to be a Brambling (Fringilla montifringilla), standing on bare earth with scattered dry leaves and twigs. The bird displays breeding male plumage characteristics: a black head and throat, bright orange-rufous breast and underparts, and black upperparts with distinct white shoulder patches and wing bars. The bill is short, conical, and appears yellowish-grey rather than solid black. The legs are pinkish-brown.
